title: feat(scripts): report-only census of ${…} authored on keys nothing evaluates (objectui#7851)
body:
Fixes #7851

A json fence in `content/docs/**` can author any key at all on a node and no gate objects. `check:doc-types` judges the `type` literal and states the exclusion in its own header — *"NOT in scope, deliberately: whether the snippet's OTHER keys are read by the renderer the type resolves to"* — and `check:doc-snippets` covers these pages but type-checks `ts`/`tsx` blocks only. So the json fence bodies were read by nothing.

This lands the instrument that reads them, **report-only**, and the census it produces.

## The census, on `59df1dab2`

```
204 json/jsonc fence(s) across 184 file(s) under content/docs
204 parsed, 0 UNPARSED          (1 of them parsed as an object BODY)
359 node(s) with a string `type`
 66 ${…} site(s) on those nodes, 49 of them carried
 17 sites author ${…} on a key nothing evaluates, across 5 pages
```

| page | sites | keys |
|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/guide/expressions.md` | 8 | `badge.variant` x3, `badge.text`, `card.body`, `card.className`, `list.items` x2 |
| `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` | 5 | `chart.data`, `badge.text`, `badge.variant`, `alert.variant`, `alert.message` |
| `content/docs/guide/architecture.md` | 2 | `badge.text`, `badge.variant` |
| `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` | 1 | `action.condition` |
| `content/docs/guide/layout.md` | 1 | `page.title` |

The 8 on `expressions.md` are an **independent reproduction** of the number objectui#7418's prototype measured on the same tree — its six sites plus the two `list.items` occurrences that card deliberately left unclaimed. The other 9, in four further pages, were not in any card's enumeration. ⛔ Nothing outside this PR's four files is touched: the other pages are reported, not repaired.

### Fence languages, and the dialect blind spot

Asked for after a sibling seat measured objectui#7440's page: its three teaching blocks are fenced ```jsonc, not ```json.

```
By fence language: json 198 (198 parsed, 0 unparsed); jsonc 6 (6 parsed, 0 unparsed)
✅  Dialect blind spot: none — no fence OUTSIDE json/jsonc parses as a JSON document holding a typed node.
```

`jsonc` was already in the scanned set, so `content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md`'s four `jsonc` fences are all counted and judged today (they produce no expression finding, because objectui#7440 is the read-back half, not this one). What was missing was the **reading** that says so, and it is now printed on every run — per language, both directions — together with a probe that parses every fence **outside** the scanned set purely to report whether it would have been a JSON document holding a typed node. A missed dialect is now a number rather than something a human finds by re-reading a page. Both are pinned.

### ⚠️ A hit is a candidate, not a verdict

`type` is not one vocabulary in these pages — `check:doc-types` measured at least seven that all spell that key — so a node from another one is judged here against a carriage map that does not govern it. One of today's 17 is exactly that: `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`'s `ActionSchema` example authors a `${…}` on `condition`, which the **action runner's** own gate evaluates, not `SchemaRenderer`'s node channels. ⛔ The obvious fix — classify by enclosing key path — was built and measured by that gate before being rejected as non-convergent, and that ruling is inherited here rather than re-litigated. Report-only is what makes inheriting it safe: a candidate a human reads costs a minute, and nothing is blocked while the corpus is read. The caveat is stated in the script's header and printed under every findings list.


## Report-only, deliberately

Three members of this class are open (objectui#7440, objectui#7444, objectui#7838). A blocking gate would go red on all of them the day it landed and turn one card into four, so the 2026-09-06 ruling on this card is that the census is the deliverable and the decision it feeds — clean the corpus first, or build a ledger — is **not made here**.

Same posture as `Changeset Overwrite Report`, and the same boundary: report-only means the gate declines to fail on its **findings**, never that it passes without looking. It exits 1 when the **instrument** is broken — a derivation that matched nothing, a missing spec artifact, a failed control. There is no `continue-on-error` on the step, because that would swallow exactly the failure that must be loud.

## Both halves of the universe are derived, never typed

| half | source | today's answer |
|---|---|---|
| carriage map | `expressionBindableTextKeysFor` out of the **built** `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0` `dist/ui/index.mjs` — the lookup `SchemaRenderer.tsx:1139` itself consumes | `card` -> `title`, `description`; `badge` / `progress` / `input` / `list` -> nothing |
| evaluated channels | `SchemaRenderer.tsx`'s own call sites — `evaluator.evaluate(newSchema.X)`, `isConfigBag(newSchema.X)`, `evaluate{Visibility,Enablement}Predicate(newSchema.X, …)` | `content`; bags `properties`, `props`; 8 condition keys |

Read from **call sites**, never from the surrounding prose: that file's comments name `visibleOn`, `disabled` and both bags many times over, and a scan of the raw text would be describing its own docblocks. Either derivation matching nothing is exit 1 — a silently narrowed universe turns correct documentation into findings.

The test cross-checks the condition keys against a **different source**: the two `VISIBILITY_SHOW_KEYS` / `VISIBILITY_HIDE_KEYS` array literals the same file declares. One source read twice proves nothing.

## Proving it can see

**Built-in controls, run before every census, not once in this PR.** The positive fixture is `guide/expressions.md`'s Status Badge block exactly as it stands on `main` — `badge` carries nothing, so `text` and `variant` are both findings. The negative fixture is a `card` using only carried channels.

```
Controls: positive fixture reported [text, variant] (expected text, variant);
          negative fixture reported nothing (expected nothing).
✅  Controls pass: this gate can see the class it is looking for, and does not cry wolf.
```

The pins **sabotage** each control too, because a control that cannot fail is not a control: widen the carriage map until the defect disappears and the positive control fails; drop `visibleOn` from the channels and the negative control fails.

**On-disk mutation control, on the real corpus.** objectui#7418's repair has not merged yet, so the six sites are still on `main` — the instrument reports them today, which is the positive direction already live. The remaining direction was measured by applying PR #7847's repair to the Status Badge block on disk and watching the census track it. The implementation was committed **before** the trap was armed.

```
HEAD blob   = 03d44a90afc4501555ec181153e2e5746256ffb6
before hash = 03d44a90afc4501555ec181153e2e5746256ffb6   (equal: tree at HEAD before the mutation)
anchor "text": "${status}"   before 1  ->  after 0
anchor "label": "Completed"  before 0  ->  after 1
after hash  = a60c2135800e165264e73408c87706990e38fcc0   (changed: the mutation reached disk)

census before   17 sites in 5 pages
census after    15 sites in 5 pages
diff            -  :353  badge.text      -  :354  badge.variant
                only other change: card.className :404 -> :399, the block shrank 5 lines
```

Restored under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with `git checkout HEAD -- "$REPO_ROOT/…"`, and proven **by state**, not by an exit code: `git status --short` empty, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git hash-object` back to `03d44a90a`, the anchor count back to 1.

## The parse surface is printed on every run

`0 unparsed` is what makes "only 17 sites" mean something, so both directions are printed. Reaching 0 over the whole tree takes four tolerances beyond `JSON.parse`, all of them removals of non-data or an envelope around it — comments, raw newlines inside `${…}` strings, trailing commas, and elision markers in the three spellings the corpus uses — plus one retry for a fence that is an object body rather than an object. None can invent a key, and each is pinned, including the case that must **not** be treated as an elision (`"placeholder": "..."` is a real value).

## The half this does not answer

This is the **expression** half — *is this key evaluated*. The wider half — *is this key read back by the renderer* — is what objectui#7440 and objectui#7444 are, and it needs the per-renderer read-point contract `check:doc-types` names as its missing piece. Neither is visible here, and objectui#7838's site lives in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, outside `content/docs/**` and so outside this census's population. All three are stated in the script's header so a green census is not misread as "the fences are correct".

## Wiring, and the obligation that comes with it

One report-only step in the `docs` job of `ci.yml`, and — objectui#3653 pins that table by command — the matching sentence in the `docs` row of `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, in the same change. `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` passes in both directions. The step inherits the job's `should_run` condition, so on a PR that changes no `content/` or `apps/site/` file the census does not run; a PR that edits only the gate is covered by the vitest pins instead. Both consequences are written down at the step.

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all four changed paths, verbatim:

> ✅ NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.
> An ordinary pull request: the normal review and merge-queue route applies.

## Verification, re-run after the final commit at `59df1dab2`

Exit codes captured by redirecting first (`cmd > log 2>&1; EXIT=$?`), never through a pipe.

```
scripts/__tests__ (vitest)   EXIT=0   105 files, 3089 tests passed (28 of them this gate's)
check:doc-types              EXIT=0   Every documented component type is registered.
check:doc-snippets           EXIT=0   Semantic phase: 456 of 456 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
check:doc-fences             EXIT=0   every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript
check:docs-route-closure     EXIT=0
check:doc-example-readers    EXIT=0   OK  80 documented symbol(s), 3944 call site(s)
check:control-bytes          EXIT=0   OK (scanned 6369 tracked text file(s))
check:entry-guard            EXIT=0   67 scripts/ file(s); 61 export bindings, 61 inert on import
check-doc-links.mjs          EXIT=0   Links are valid across 17 scan roots.
type-check:scripts           EXIT=0
lint:root (eslint)           EXIT=0   249 files, 0 errors, 33 pre-existing warnings, 0 from the new files
lint:coverage                EXIT=0   46/46 packages linted
```

`check:doc-snippets` first returned **EXIT=2**, which its own output declares is *"I could not run, NOT I ran and found errors"* — read as NOT MEASURED. Its scoped build (`turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2`, 34/34 tasks) then took it to a real green.

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — EXIT=0, verdict verbatim:

> ✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.

Acted on: no changeset added, no label touched.

**Not run, said plainly:** `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint` across all 46 packages) and the repo-wide test suite. The `lint:root` scan above **is** the eslint population that contains these files — measured from eslint's own config at 249 files, with both new files present in it and clean — and this diff adds no file to any package, so no package's lint or test population moves. CI runs the farm regardless.

Session, in prose because a markdown-link footer does not survive an edit: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01KbJQ1y1J12nZxYzFWhP8Q3`
